hero.lead: A nation of 11.0 million where citizens abroad send home three tenths of the economy, two thirds of the power is renewable, and the World Bank finances roads and transparency.

capital.heading: Remittances and roads, and schools to match.

register.name: Sovereign bond, 6.4% due July 2036
register.detail: Secretaría de Finanzas · 6.4% notes due July 2036 · Legislative Decree 62-2026 · offering circular of 2026
register.note: Listed by the Secretaría de Finanzas with its 2026 offering circular and placement presentation
register.text: An international bond of the Republic of Honduras paying 6.4% and maturing in July 2036, authorised by Legislative Decree 62-2026 and listed by the Secretaría de Finanzas with its 2026 offering circular. The proceeds go to the central government, whose budget carries public spending on the seven standards.

register.name: Thematic green, social and sustainable sovereign bond, reopening
register.detail: Secretaría de Finanzas · 8.625% notes due November 2034 · reopened in 2025 for US$200M · US$900M outstanding at 30 June 2026
register.note: Proceeds for government programmes and projects with positive social and environmental impacts, in line with the Sustainable Development Goals
register.text: The Government reopened its thematic green, social and sustainable sovereign bond, the 8.625% notes due November 2034, for US$200 million in 2025; the issue stood at US$900 million at 30 June 2026. The Secretaría de Finanzas states that the reopening finances government programmes and projects meant to generate positive social and environmental impacts, in line with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. It links sovereign borrowing to social and environmental results.

register.name: Supplementary financing, Development Policy Financing on Fiscal and Climate Transparency and Sustainability
register.detail: World Bank · signed in the second quarter of 2026 · executed by the Secretaría de Finanzas
register.note: Adds to the US$145.3M first operation of February 2025
register.text: Supplementary financing from the World Bank to the first development policy financing on fiscal and climate transparency and sustainability, signed by the Secretaría de Finanzas in the second quarter of 2026. It is budget support: the funds go to the general budget, which carries public spending on the seven standards.

register.name: Resilient Management of the CA-13 Road Corridor, La Ceiba to Puerto Castilla
register.detail: World Bank · loan 7879-HN · press release 10 July 2025 · contract start 13 August 2025 · disbursement deadline 31 December 2033
register.note: Co-financed by Spain (ICO, FONPRODE) with US$79.9M
register.text: A US$100 million World Bank loan for the resilient management of the CA-13 road corridor between La Ceiba and Puerto Castilla in northern Honduras, executed by SIT; no disbursement was recorded by the end of 2025. It serves livelihood, by connecting people to work, markets and services.

register.name: Gender Equality and Social Inclusion Programme
register.detail: OPEC Fund · loan 16404PL · contract start 1 July 2025 · disbursement deadline 29 May 2026 · executed by the Secretaría de Finanzas
register.note: The OPEC Fund disbursed US$50.8M to Honduras in the first half of 2026
register.text: A US$50 million sector loan from the OPEC Fund for International Development for the Gender Equality and Social Inclusion Programme, executed by the Secretaría de Finanzas. It finances the budget in support of policies for women and excluded groups, and bears on livelihood.

register.name: First Development Policy Financing on Fiscal and Climate Transparency and Sustainability
register.detail: World Bank · loans 7703-HN and 7702-HN · press release and contract start 17 February 2025 · US$145.3M · disbursement deadline 29 May 2026
register.note: Supplementary financing of US$125M signed in the second quarter of 2026
register.text: A US$145.3 million development policy financing from the World Bank, with a contract start of 17 February 2025, executed by the Secretaría de Finanzas, to promote fiscal and climate transparency and sustainability. It is budget support: the funds go to the general budget, which carries public spending on the seven standards.

register.name: Sustainable Connectivity Project
register.detail: World Bank · loan 7672-HN · approved 17 December 2024 · contract start 18 December 2024 · disbursement deadline 31 December 2031
register.note: US$0.3M disbursed by the end of 2025
register.text: A US$187 million World Bank loan for the connectivity and resilience of the road network of north-western Honduras, executed by SIT. It serves livelihood, by connecting people to work, markets and services.

register.name: INNOVASAN: innovation, resilience and sustainability of agrifood systems in the north-centre
register.detail: IFAD · loan 2000005030 · contract start 4 September 2024 · disbursement deadline 4 March 2034
register.note: A further IFAD loan of US$10.0M (2000005029) starts the same day
register.text: A US$7.7 million loan from the International Fund for Agricultural Development for the Project to Strengthen Innovation, Resilience and Sustainability of Agrifood Systems in the North-Centre of Honduras (INNOVASAN). It serves the food and livelihood standards; no disbursement was recorded by the end of 2025.

register.name: Extended Fund Facility and Extended Credit Facility
register.detail: IMF · approved 21 September 2023 · 36 months · SDR 624.5M · fourth and fifth reviews completed 29 June 2026 · about US$725M (SDR 535.3M) disbursed
register.note: The authorities requested a short extension to complete the sixth and final reviews
register.text: Two 36-month IMF arrangements totalling about US$847 million (SDR 624.5 million), approved on 21 September 2023. On 29 June 2026 the Executive Board completed the fourth and fifth reviews, releasing about US$242 million (SDR 178.4 million) and bringing disbursements to about US$725 million. The programme supports fiscal discipline, the reorganisation of social spending to protect vulnerable households and climate resilience.

register.name: Towards More Inclusive Education: Transforming the Rural School
register.detail: IDB · signed in the second quarter of 2026 · executed by the Secretaría de Educación
register.note: Education is the standard furthest from reach in Honduras
register.text: A US$55 million loan from the Inter-American Development Bank, signed in the second quarter of 2026 and executed by the Secretaría de Educación, for the programme Towards More Inclusive Education: Transforming the Rural School. It serves education, the standard furthest from reach: on 2019 data, 79.3% of children in Honduras could not read a simple text by the end of primary school.

register.name: Fiscal Strengthening Programme for Inclusive Growth
register.detail: IDB · signed in the second quarter of 2026 · executed by the Secretaría de Finanzas
register.note: Signed with the World Bank supplementary financing: US$280M of external loans in the quarter
register.text: A US$100 million loan from the Inter-American Development Bank for the Fiscal Strengthening Programme for Inclusive Growth, signed in the second quarter of 2026 and executed by the Secretaría de Finanzas. It is budget support: the funds go to the general budget, which carries public spending on the seven standards.

register.name: Western Corridor CA-4, Chamelecón to Naco: widening, rehabilitation and improvement
register.detail: CAF · contract start 16 October 2025 · disbursement deadline 22 October 2031 · executed by SIT
register.note: No disbursement recorded by the end of 2025
register.text: A US$160 million loan from CAF, the development bank of Latin America and the Caribbean, to widen, rehabilitate and improve the CA-4 Western Corridor between Chamelecón and Naco. It serves livelihood, by connecting people to work, markets and services.

register.name: Coffee Bonus Programme for Small and Medium Producers
register.detail: CAF · contract start 16 October 2025 · disbursement deadline 16 April 2027 · executed by the Secretaría de Agricultura y Ganadería
register.text: A US$10 million loan from CAF for the Programa Bono Cafetero, in support of small and medium coffee producers, executed by the Secretaría de Agricultura y Ganadería. It serves livelihood for coffee-farming families.

register.name: Sustainable Recovery of Lake Yojoa Programme
register.detail: CABEI · loan 2336 · contract start 20 December 2024 · disbursement deadline 5 July 2031
register.note: No disbursement recorded by the end of 2025
register.text: A US$80 million loan from the Central American Bank for Economic Integration for the Programme for the Sustainable Recovery of Lake Yojoa. It serves the water standard, through the recovery of the lake and its basin.

register.name: El Tablón Multipurpose Dam, Stage I
register.detail: CABEI · loan 2342 · contract start 17 December 2024 · disbursement deadline 18 February 2031
register.note: No disbursement recorded by the end of 2025
register.text: A US$300 million loan from the Central American Bank for Economic Integration for the construction of the first stage of the El Tablón multipurpose dam. A multipurpose dam stores water for several uses, such as supply, irrigation, flood control and power, and so bears on the water, food and energy standards.

register.name: Honduras Resilient Roads Programme (PCR-HN)
register.detail: CABEI · loan 2333 · contract start 14 December 2023 · disbursement deadline 31 October 2029 · 12.5% disbursed at the end of 2025
register.note: A further US$96.3M (loan 2335) finances section B-1, the El Progreso bypass, from 5 August 2024
register.text: A US$607 million loan from the Central American Bank for Economic Integration for the Honduras Resilient Roads Programme; US$75.9 million had been disbursed by the end of 2025. It serves livelihood, by connecting people to work, markets and services.

register.name: Hospital Network Support Programme (PARH)
register.detail: CABEI · loan 2329 · contract start 14 December 2023 · disbursement deadline 31 July 2028 · 43.7% disbursed at the end of 2025
register.note: US$54.8M disbursed by the end of 2025
register.text: A US$125.4 million loan from the Central American Bank for Economic Integration for the Programme of Support to the Hospital Network of the Republic of Honduras. It serves the health standard.

register.name: Resilient Management of the CA-13 Road Corridor, co-financing
register.detail: Spain, ICO (FONPRODE) · contract start 7 August 2025 · disbursement deadline 31 December 2033 · alongside World Bank loan 7879-HN
register.note: The Secretaría de Finanzas annual debt report gives US$79.8M
register.text: Spain’s FONPRODE, through the Instituto de Crédito Oficial (ICO), co-finances with the World Bank the resilient management of the CA-13 road corridor between La Ceiba and Puerto Castilla. It serves livelihood, by connecting people to work, markets and services.

register.name: Hospital Network Strengthening Project
register.detail: JICA · loan HO-P7 · contract start 20 March 2024 · disbursement deadline 20 March 2030 · 0.2% disbursed at the end of 2025
register.note: Amount as recorded in US dollars by the Secretaría de Finanzas
register.text: A US$75 million loan from the Japan International Cooperation Agency to strengthen the hospital network of Honduras. It serves the health standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Diaspora
items.label: Of GDP sent home by citizens abroad, 2025
items.text: Citizens abroad send home a steady share of the economy: a flow that can back long-term finance.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 30.3% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: Hábitat para la Humanidad Honduras
items.text: A non-profit that builds and improves homes and offers credit for homes and land repaid in affordable instalments: between 2022 and December 2025 it laid 2,972 concrete floors in Honduras for 14,860 people, at an estimated L13,000 a floor with families contributing unskilled labour, and it aims at 9,160 floors by 2028.

items.name: Proyecto Mirador
items.text: A clean cooking non-profit, begun in 2004, that builds improved cookstoves in homes from materials the families provide and earns carbon credits under the Gold Standard for its Honduras programme; it has installed 400,000 stoves in Honduras and Guatemala, reaching more than 1.6 million people, and in 2026 received an AA rating from Calyx Global.

items.name: ASHONPLAFA (Asociación Hondureña de Planificación de Familia)
items.text: A non-governmental organisation that provides sexual and reproductive health care, including family planning, through clinical medical programmes, social marketing and community services; it has committed to serve 400,000 women and 60,000 young people and adolescents with family planning, 15% more than it serves now.

items.name: Café Orgánico Marcala (COMSA)
items.text: A social enterprise of coffee growers in Marcala, La Paz, focused on environmental stewardship, economic justice and human development; in 2025 it began work with Lutheran World Relief to bring training, equipment and advice on sustainable production and crop diversification to 1,500 farming families in La Paz and Intibucá.

items.name: Cooperativa ELGA (Coopelga)
items.text: A savings and credit cooperative, described by IDB Invest as the cooperative with the most assets in Honduras, with a majority female membership; it supports women to become micro-entrepreneurs and in 2024 began work with IDB Invest on a strategy to finance small and medium enterprises led or owned by women.
